correctness.rationale: For Ω<=3, divisor counts must be in {1,2,3,4,6,8}. If m<n and mτ(m)=nτ(n), then τ(m)>τ(n) and τ(n)>1; enumerated all 10 strict divisor-count pairs (3,2),(4,2),(4,3),(6,2),(6,3),(6,4),(8,2),(8,3),(8,4),(8,6). Prime-power or squarefree factorization eliminates nine. In (6,4), m=p²q and n=3m/2: integrality forces 2|m. If the squared prime is 2, n has wrong divisor count; if q=2, m=2p²,n=3p² and τ(n)=4 precisely p=3, giving 18,27. Includes 1 and primes. A separate sieve independently checked all Ω<=3 inputs through 250,000 and found only 108↔18,27, without extrapolation.

evidence: Database records occurrence of 18/27 and repeated values; does not quantify over all integers with Omega<=3 or prove exclusion
